items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1958-06-09
items.q: NAACP through Bill Handy, trying to give the Negro culture into the music field.

ctx.x: Well, that'll show you what kind of people that the jazz club has and at the head of it. He wrote me in 1949 that I have proof that we were the original Dixieland jazz band. Now he's writing up on this guy that he is the original Dixieland jazz band. They give him a cup for his presence of being in the jazz club. What wonderful people they have in New Orleans. All they were doing was to start integration, what they call the mixing bowl. They had started that up north 22 years ago, 20 years ago, by Marshall Stein.…

This is a letter headed Dominique James Nicola Rocca, 2218 Constant Street, New Orleans, Louisiana, 13, January the 9th, 1955. Senator Eastland of Mississippi, Washington, D.C. Honorable Senator Eastland, Hoping you may direct your committee attention to the propaganda that has been going on in New Orleans. Because wherever there is smoke, there must be fire. These people have given out history, read jazz music, as compiled by the Northern Coppetbaggers, NAACP through Bill Handy, trying to give the Negro culture…
I want you to read this here about a nine-man court.

items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1958-05-26
items.q: I know where I got it. That good musician can't say that. It's different. Well, I believe that they got it from the quadrill when I see the sheet music. You know, that makes sense. You've never seen it? No, I've never seen the sheet music. No. I'm gonna tell you what it is. It's all lies concocted b

ctx.x: Sure. Well, nobody will hear this, ya know. We can save it, ya know. And, uh, put it down. Right. Put it down. Right. Put it down.

By blowing the cornet, I was making this. Da, And by forcing, the back part would go. You understand what I mean? I see. And that gave me an idea of putting that into the throat. And I tried to make that on the horn, and I made it on the horn. On the horn. See, on this cornet. Not this one. The one that I had was a little bit. A piece of junk. Now, that's the whole tiger rag in completion. It has a little part of the quadrill. And if anyone says they have it in there, you play the tiger, if you played the tiger…

He wouldn't even play jazz or the blues. He'd committed to paper. This Negro here had went into the hands of the receiver. And I know this tune by the name of Jobo Blues. And I used to play it in the band. And Russell Roberts says to me, you know whose tune that is? I said, no. He says, that's Hannity's tune. I says, it's a damn good tune. I said, let me go and see him. I may be able to record it for him. At that time, he was in the hands of the receiver. I went on over there. And he wasn't there. I spoke to his…
